results.evidence: `resolve_untagged_followup_mode` now returns `stored_untagged_followup_mode(...) or UntaggedFollowupMode.ASK`, and `stored_...` returns None for no row or empty column (`if not stored: return None`). Unset users now resolve to ASK, which already leads to the ask prompt. The webhook gate that only drops NEVER isn't shown, so this relies on the author's account of it.
Stored valid values still resolve via `UntaggedFollowupMode(stored)`. AUTO, NEVER and ASK are unchanged, and only the unset case moved to ASK.

The prompt keeps 'Yes, take a look' and 'No thanks'. When `offer_default` is true it adds 'Yes, and always do this' (saves AUTO) and 'No, and don't ask again' (saves NEVER). The defaults only appear when the replier is the thread creator with no stored choice. That fits the setting living on the creator's row.

`_untagged_followups_section_blocks(mode)` takes a mode and can render ASK as `initial_option`. The caller that decides whether to render the section for users with no row isn't shown and the patch doesn't change it. So I can't confirm the section is no longer omitted.

In `stored_untagged_followup_mode`, a non-empty value not in `UntaggedFollowupMode.values` returns `UntaggedFollowupMode.NEVER`. The resolver's `or ASK` doesn't override it, because the NEVER enum member is truthy.
The prompt only has plain text: "Change it any time on the PostHog Home tab." It never calls `app_home_url`, though that is imported. There is no link and no fallback logic.
The patch has no changes to quota or credits handling, and no distinction between unconfirmed untagged replies and mentions or confirmed replies in denial messaging.

result:
Unset thread follow-up now resolves to "ask", and the prompt can save a default. I didn't run any tests, and I didn't add a test for the new prompt buttons.

- **Default behavior** (`services/slack_settings.py`): a user with no saved setting now gets the "ask" behavior instead of "never". The webhook only drops "never", so their untagged replies now reach the classifier and then the prompt. Anyone with a saved setting behaves as before, including a value we've since retired, which still means "never". I added `stored_untagged_followup_mode` to tell "never chose" apart from an actual choice. I also updated the comments in `models.py`, but not the `help_text`, so no migration is needed.
- **Prompt with a save option** (`api.py`): when the replier is the thread creator and has no saved choice, the prompt gets a second row of buttons. "Yes, and always do this" sends the reply and saves "auto". "No, and don't ask again" drops the reply and saves "never". Each save re-checks that the setting is still unset, so it never overwrites a choice made in the meantime.
- **Home page**: the existing "Thread follow-ups" picker already lets people change the setting. It now shows "Ask them first" for people who haven't chosen, and I updated its docstring. There is no visual distinction between "chose ask" and "never chose", and the note in the prompt says the default can be changed on the Home tab.
- **Tests**: I updated `tests/services/test_slack_settings.py` so that no row or a NULL value resolves to "ask". I did not check whether `test_thread_message_routing.py` or `test_untagged_followup_interactivity.py` assume the old "never" default for unset users.

One behavior to know about: the follow-up setting belongs to whoever started the thread, so the save buttons only appear when the replier is that person. Someone else replying in that thread gets the plain yes/no prompt.
